Here is what I can rigorously support with real URLs, dates, and labels. Wherever I could not find a genuine founder/company statement or a real user/forum post on the specific point, I mark it explicitly as **NOT FOUND**. I do **not** invent numbers; anything without a URL is marked “unsourced”.

---

## 1. Founder / company statements about churn, retention, and why subscribers cancel

### Brain.fm – Dan Clark (CEO) on retention and annual vs monthly plans

**Claim (FIRST-PARTY):** Annual plans create more committed “power users” and improve retention compared to monthly subscribers.

- In a Mixergy interview with Andrew Warner, Brain.fm CEO **Dan Clark** explicitly links yearly plans to higher retention and more committed usage: “So our retention goes up, right, because people are trying something, and then two, I think it’s a commitment thing. So people that buy yearly become power users within eight days and people that buy monthly, they’re kind of like just trying it.”  
  - Source (podcast transcript, Mixergy) – December 20, 2019 – **Mixergy (interview, not a forum)**  
  - URL: `https://mixergy.com/interviews/brain-fm-with-dan-clark/`[16]  
  - Label: **FIRST-PARTY**

**Claim (FIRST-PARTY):** As of late 2019, Brain.fm reported about 150,000 active users, ~85,000 lifetime accounts, ~30,000+ subscription accounts, and “close to 2 million” in recurring revenue.

- In the same Mixergy interview, Clark states: “So we have about **150,000 active users**. We have a lot of people actually on **lifetime accounts, almost 85,000**. We have about **30,000 plus or so on subscription accounts**… What did you say your revenue was? Dan: It’s **close to 2 million**. Andrew: Two million, recurring revenue? Dan: Yep.”  
  - Source – December 31, 2019 (Mixergy page date) – **Mixergy (interview)**  
  - URL: `https://mixergy.com/interviews/brain-fm-with-dan-clark/`[4]  
  - Label: **FIRST-PARTY**

**Why subscribers cancel (Brain.fm):**  
- Specific, direct founder statements about *why* subscribers cancel (price vs boredom vs stopped use) **NOT FOUND** in accessible public interviews and posts. The Mixergy interview focuses on growth, enterprise, and plan structure, not exit reasons.  
- Mark: **NOT FOUND**.

---

### Endel – company statements (MAU, listening hours)

**Claim (FIRST-PARTY):** Endel reports “over 1 million” monthly active users and ~1.5 million monthly listening hours.

- Endel’s official site “Team” page states: “The ecosystem has **over 1 million active users monthly**, and they listen to a **million and a half hours a month**.”  
  - Source – page last updated August 26, 2026 – **Endel website (company page)**  
  - URL: `https://endel.io/about`[9]  
  - Label: **FIRST-PARTY**

- TechCrunch coverage of Endel’s April 2022 funding round quotes similar figures: “Founded in 2018, Endel has **more than 1 million monthly active users and over 1.5 million monthly listening hours**.”  
  - Source – April 5, 2022 – **TechCrunch**  
  - URL: `https://techcrunch.com/2022/04/05/endel-raises-15m-to-further-develop-its-ai-powered-sound-wellness-technology/`[15]  
  - Label: **THIRD-PARTY-ESTIMATE** (press, echoing company numbers)

- Music Ally’s report on Endel’s funding similarly notes: “Endel now has **more than one million monthly active users** of its apps, and those users are listening to **1.5m hours of music a month**.”  
  - Source – April 6, 2022 – **Music Ally**  
  - URL: `https://musically.com/2022/04/06/ai-music-startup-endel-raises-15m-in-latest-funding-round/`[12]  
  - Label: **THIRD-PARTY-ESTIMATE** (press using company data)

**Why subscribers cancel / churn insights (Endel):**

- I could **not** find any public founder interview (Oleg Stavitsky, Dmitry Evgrafov) or blog post that directly discusses *why* Endel’s subscribers cancel (e.g., “bored,” “price,” “stopped using”). Searches return help-center instructions on *how* to cancel but not *why people cancel*.  
- Example help-center article explains cancellation mechanics, not reasons: “You want to cancel your subscription” describes auto-renewal and app/Store flows.  
  - Source – January 1, 2024 (article date) – **Endel Help Center (Zendesk)**  
  - URL: `https://endel.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/360003562239-You-want-to-cancel-your-subscription`[18]  
  - Label: **FIRST-PARTY** (support documentation, but not about “why”)  

- Mark for explicit “why cancel / retention” comments by founders: **NOT FOUND**.

---

### Focus@Will – Will Henshall on usage, retention-like behavior

**Claim (FIRST-PARTY):** In one client organization, about 25% of users were consistent Focus@Will users.

- On the “B2B Launcher” podcast, Will Henshall describes a Google Ads agency deployment: “Will recently signed up a Google Ads marketing agency with about 120 users. **About 25 percent of those users use the service consistently.**”  
  - Source – July 1, 2021 – **B2B Launcher podcast show notes**  
  - URL: `https://b2blauncher.com/episode264/`[23]  
  - Label: **FIRST-PARTY** (founder describing engagement; this is not formal retention, but usage consistency)

**Claim (FIRST-PARTY / THIRD-PARTY-ESTIMATE):** Focus@Will has “over 2 million users” / “nearly 1 million users”.

- The Medical Futurist’s Patreon post describes Focus@Will: “With **over 2 million users** it now helps people at work and study to reduce distractions and be more productive.”  
  - Source – April 22, 2021 – **The Medical Futurist (Patreon article)**  
  - URL: `https://www.patreon.com/posts/making-you-more-50339540`[25]  
  - Label: **THIRD-PARTY-ESTIMATE** (press-like content; number likely comes from the founder but not clearly attributed)
